A handle is a claim you can always cash

content.value: The retrieval half of the Barkpark context-compression doctrine: brief views may drop bulk only because every card names its higher authority — a
= doc id + rev, resolved by a plain GET against the CMS itself, TTL infinite. This paper specifies that doctrine to charter grade, designs
bp park
for foreign bulk, and rules on MCP resource_link. Verdict: roughly 70% of the machinery already exists on the wire — the epic is three builds plus legislation, not new infrastructure. Crown paper:
ctx-compression-capstone
A handle is
{doc_id, type, rev}
. The store is the CMS. TTL is infinite. Resolution is
bp doc get
. Headroom needs max-retrieval-rounds and a 5-minute cache because its store can lie; ours cannot — resolution returns full truth or 404s honestly, so round limits dissolve into byte-honesty plus
--fields
narrowing.

content.value: Six laws that make the doctrine ratifiable, then six buildable slices. Where the evidence decides, the law is stated as decided; where it does not, the fork is named in Risks & unknowns and left to you.

rows.value: A handle is the JSON triple
{doc_id, type, rev}
carried with an executable escape-hatch command (AXI help[] style, real ids). It is NOT a universal URI:
barkpark://
stays MCP-resource-space only; tenancy context binds resolution (lane 4's ruling).
help[] precedent shipped in AXI wave 1; the
{"_ref": id}
reference grammar already accepts bare ids (expand.ex:247) — the handle extends it, no parallel $ref invented.
rev is the existing opaque CAS token — 16 random bytes hex, regenerated per write. A handle is fresh or moved-on; never 'n revisions behind'.
writer.ex generate_rev = strong_rand_bytes(16) — unordered by construction.
Resolution returns current truth + _rev; a mismatch with the handle's rev is a loud staleness signal, not a failure. True rev-pinned retrieval is EXPLICITLY DEFERRED; the archaeology hatch is
GET /v1/data/revision/:dataset/:id
(already Envelope.redact-sealed).
Revision rows key on their own UUID and never store the rev string (revision.ex) — pinning by CAS rev is unbuildable without a schema change, and no consumer needs it yet.
Bare
rev
always means the document CAS 32-hex string. Papers' monotonic streaming int (
content["rev"]
) is always qualified — it appears only as bulldocs.patch
--if-rev
(typed int) and may never be abbreviated to bare rev on any new surface.
The census found the split is clean today but purely by accident — no written rule exists, and a generic 'pass if-rev to guard your write' helper would silently break across the two systems.
Handle-resolution output is never re-briefed or re-compressed, and a miss is a terminal, actionable error ('gone — re-run the source'), never a retryable 404.
Headroom #1077: the proxy compressed its own retrieve responses — a literal infinite loop. #1776: a non-terminal miss error drove one agent to retry a dead hash 25× in 11 minutes.
Infinite TTL means no TTL cliff — not no GC. Park GC is loud, two-stage (flag → grace → delete), per-dataset, every stage evented.
Headroom #714 (5-min TTL kills long jobs) and #1809 (restart wipes the in-memory store) are the two most-cited failures in its tracker; PlaygroundReaper is our in-house two-stage model.

blocks.text: ETag: a port, not an invention

content.value: Premise corrected by the storm:
/v1/data

doc reads ALREADY have ETag/304 — QueryController uses the doc's _rev verbatim as a strong ETag (doc_etag) and a sha256 over id:rev pairs for lists (list_etag). What's missing is the Tasks plugin controller: /v1/tasks, /prime, /events have zero conditional-GET today. The port:

items.value: Extract a shared
BarkparkWeb.ETag
helper (etag_matches?/strip_etag) instead of duplicating QueryController's.
Task list_etag MUST fold
view=brief|full

and shaping params into the hash — QueryController's formula hashes only id:rev, so two different representations of the same docs collide today (latent RFC 9110 violation; no Vary header exists anywhere — add one).
Single-task show reuses rev directly as the ETag — the free handle-doctrine win.
Client: GetConditional exists and is proven; taskboard's getJSON hardcodes an empty If-None-Match (throws the ETag away by design) — wire a per-URL cache keyed sha256(baseURL+token+path+query).
Do not copy the known cost blindly: the ETag is computed AFTER the full query+render, so a 304 saves wire only (task ppr-edge-cache-verdict names this). The events feed needs no ETag at all — its
since=
cursor is already the cheaper freshness primitive and can short-circuit BEFORE the DB replay.
GetConditionalBounded is UNCOMMITTED local work in this checkout (internal/apiclient) — the slice must absorb or await it, never duplicate it.

blocks.text: What we learned

content.value: (1) 'The CAS seam has known holes' — no longer true: both were FIXED and merged before this run (batch If-Match drop → PR #2381; CLI --if-rev no-op → PR #5720). The doctrine stands on an audited, closed seam — cite as proof, file no slices. (2) 'Doc reads emit no ETag' — this lane's own miss: QueryController has full ETag/304 on /v1/data; only the Tasks controller lacks it. (3) 'Dual-carry resource_link is harmless' — wild clients crash, not ignore. (4) Headroom drift: 504 open issues (not 256); max_retrieval_rounds appears nowhere in its tracker; no true hash collision exists there — the real cluster is TTL cliffs, format drift, silent store rejects. (5) Fleet-scale spend REVERSES the 12-session pilot: result bytes 71.8% vs input 26.4% — park aims at the bigger side after all.
Headroom's issue tracker, mined issue-by-issue, is the strongest external validation the doctrine has: every major retrieval failure it documents is impossible here
, not by discipline.

is latest-with-rev-honesty enough for the whole epic? Evidence says yes (the board needs latest + events), but adding a rev column to revisions in wave 1 is cheap if you disagree — say so before the charter freezes.
opt-in now + smoke test, or defer entirely until one target client proves auto-follow. The URI-space extension is safe either way.

parked docs stay leaves (recommendation), or a same-dataset receipt doc in production linking task→park? The leaf design costs discoverability; the evidence (edges fail closed cross-dataset) makes the leaf free and the alternative a new build.

What we learned

Premises that fell (1) 'The CAS seam has known holes' — no longer true: both were FIXED and merged before this run (batch If-Match drop → PR #2381; CLI --if-rev no-op → PR #5720). The doctrine stands on an audited, closed seam — cite as proof, file no slices. (2) 'Doc reads emit no ETag' — this lane's own miss: QueryController has full ETag/304 on /v1/data; only the Tasks controller lacks it. (3) 'Dual-carry resource_link is harmless' — wild clients crash, not ignore. (4) Headroom drift: 504 open issues (not 256); max_retrieval_rounds appears nowhere in its tracker; no true hash collision exists there — the real cluster is TTL cliffs, format drift, silent store rejects. (5) Fleet-scale spend REVERSES the 12-session pilot: result bytes 71.8% vs input 26.4% — park aims at the bigger side after all.

Risks & unknowns

Judgment calls explicitly left to you:

  1. Park: plugin or host-core? Recommendation: plugin (the tasks precedent — universally present, severable). The doctrine wants park everywhere agents run; the plugin doctrine wants Barkpark whole without it. Tasks themselves are a plugin, so precedent supports the recommendation.
  2. Park body ceiling: 2 MB recommended; 256 KB–2 MB all defensible for JSONB rows. Above-ceiling behavior is refuse-with-pointer, never silent truncate.
  3. Mandatory --summary vs auto-fallback (recommendation: mandatory — honesty is the product).
  4. Accept the 76-byte hostile-tripwire squeak for brief v3, or bump the ceiling with a recorded why.
  5. Pinning deferral: is latest-with-rev-honesty enough for the whole epic? Evidence says yes (the board needs latest + events), but adding a rev column to revisions in wave 1 is cheap if you disagree — say so before the charter freezes.
  6. resource_link timing: opt-in now + smoke test, or defer entirely until one target client proves auto-follow. The URI-space extension is safe either way.
  7. Graph provenance: parked docs stay leaves (recommendation), or a same-dataset receipt doc in production linking task→park? The leaf design costs discoverability; the evidence (edges fail closed cross-dataset) makes the leaf free and the alternative a new build.
Handed to lane 4 (security/tenancy) — the doctrine is incomplete without these Can a handle cash across workspaces, or does resolution always bind to the caller's tenancy context? What context binds MCP-server-token resolution (the server holds one token — whose workspace)? What WriteScope governs bp park writes into a dedicated dataset? And are member-open revision reads (the archaeology hatch) right for parked foreign bulk, which may carry rawer material than authored content?

Residual risks: (1) porting the ETag pattern also ports its known cost — 304s still pay the full query+render; fine for wave 1, named so nobody calls it a cache win it isn't. (2) Media is not a safe overflow target for park until it has GC — the refuse-with-pointer design depends on a human in the loop. (3) The MCP surface is essentially unexercised in the fleet corpus (4 calls ever, all task_ready) — the 48 KB clamp and any resource_link behavior need deliberate exercise sessions, not history mining. (4) brief v2's merge-machinery starvation (seconds-truncated updated_at, claim-dropped-when-empty) is taskboard-flagship's territory — rev on the card helps but does not close it; do not double-file.
